text:
Maria Chen: Heads-up — last night we had two customers get increased 429s because their primary model pool hit sustained saturation. Thinking we should implement an automatic model-variant fallback triggered by a capacity signal (not just latency). Thoughts?
Kevin Park: Yep saw those alerts. Important to distinguish transient spikes vs sustained saturation — do we want a simple threshold or a more smoothed signal (p50/p95 of queue length over 30s)? :thinking:
Soumya Rao: I vote for smoothed signal + cooldown window. Otherwise we flip-flop and lose cache locality. Maybe: if capacity_util > 0.92 for 45s -> trigger fallback for X seconds.
Luca Ferraro: Also need to consider cost/quality tradeoffs. Fallback may pick a cheaper/quantized variant which could degrade output. We need a per-customer policy: some customers prefer availability over quality.
Amy Patel: Product: can we expose a toggle in Console per-api-key: "Allow capacity fallback" + a selector for fallback preference (quality|cost|latency)? Should default to latency for free-tier and quality for enterprise unless they opt-in.
Kevin Park: Implementation note: we already route by tier/region. Adding capacity-driven variant fallback should be a policy layer that runs after routing decision but before enqueue. We should add a short-circuit: if primary_model.pool_util > threshold -> rewrite model_hint to fallback_variant.
Soumya Rao: API-wise, two options: 1) add route.preferred_model and route.fallback_policy (explicit) in internal routing API, or 2) surface a runtime signal (capacity_overflow=true) and let inference service decide. I prefer (1) for deterministic audits.
Luca Ferraro: +1 for explicit fallback_policy config. Helps tracing: which policy caused the switch. Telemetry needs to record "fallback_reason=capacity" and original_model.
Maria Chen: Good point — telemetry must include: original_model, chosen_model, reason, tenant_id, decision_ts, cooldown_until. We want dashboards showing fallback frequency per-tenant.
Kevin Park: Also keep quota semantics clear: if we fallback to cheaper variant, do we still charge the customer the price of the primary? Product decision. For Dedicated, probably same seat-based billing, for hosted per-token maybe charge chosen model. Need billing and legal loop. @Amy Patel
Amy Patel: Noted. We'll draft billing options. For now default to charge for actual serving model; enterprise can opt into primary-priced SLA.
Soumya Rao: UX for rollouts: when we flip fallback_policy, we should allow canary targeting (5% tenants) and ramp. Console should show per-tenant metrics and an "impact preview" (estimated cost delta and quality regression) before applying org-wide.
Luca Ferraro: For the runtime change, propose adding these fields to routing API: 
```
{
  "model": "redwood/gptx-16k",
  "fallback_policy": {
    "type": "capacity",
    "threshold": 0.92,
    "smoothing_secs": 45,
    "cooldown_secs": 120,
    "variants": ["redwood/gptx-16k-quant","redwood/gptx-8k-quant"]
  }
}
```
Routing layer evaluates and rewrites request.model if triggered.
Maria Chen: Love that. Make sure variants are ordered by preference and we record which variant chosen. Also need a circuit breaker: if latency/quality post-fallback is worse on average, revert for that tenant.
Kevin Park: How do we measure "quality" automatically? We have eval sets but not per-tenant gold. Could track downstream error rates or user-reported regressions. For initial rollout, use simple metrics: increase in completions_per_prompt latency and rate of short completions.
Jen Ortiz: From Ops side — alerting rules: 1) high fallback rate for a tenant (>5% of requests) 2) sudden spike in fallback-related errors 3) fallback churn (flip-flop) — should trigger on-call. Add these to runbook.
OpsBot: deploy-bot: feature branch pushed: feature/fallback-policy-api. CI: build passed, integration tests queued.
Soumya Rao: Integration tests should simulate hot-path: fake pool_util and assert rewrite occurs and telemetry emitted. Also test cooldown and smoothing.
Luca Ferraro: Will add telemetry events: `fallback_decision` with tags [tenant, original_model, chosen_variant, reason, smoothing_window, cooldown_until]. Dashboard: per-tenant heatmap + time-series for fallback rate.
Amy Patel: UX mock: Console -> Routing -> Model fallback -> per-route toggle -> canary slider -> preview panel. I'll drop a mock in #design later today.
Maria Chen: Decision summary: implement explicit fallback_policy on route, use smoothed capacity signal (configurable), record telemetry with detailed tags, console toggle + canary UX, add runbook alerts. Action items: 
- Soumya: design API and tests (ETA 2d)
- Luca: telemetry schema + dashboard (ETA 3d)
- Kevin: runtime routing changes + integration (ETA 5d)
- Amy: console mock + billing options (ETA 3d)
- Jen: update runbook and alerts (ETA 2d)
Maria Chen: If no objections I'll schedule a quick sync tomorrow 11a to review mocks and API sketches. :thumbsup:
Kevin Park: +1
Luca Ferraro: +1
Soumya Rao: +1
Amy Patel: +1
Jen Ortiz: +1
OpsBot: deploy-bot: branch merged to staging at 1769993050.
Maria Chen: Great, thanks everyone. We'll iterate after canary results.
